Issues.Title: refactor(docs-infra): use the router's platform Navigation API integration
Issues.Body:
adev had a hand-rolled adapter (`initializeNavigationAdapter`) that intercepted a Navigation API `navigate` event on every Router navigation and resolved/rejected it around the view transition and navigation end, so the browser could show a loading indicator on the tab and visitors could cancel a navigation with the stop button or the escape key.

The Router now provides this natively with
`withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`, which drives the Router through the Navigation API, aborts the Router navigation when the navigate event is aborted (stop button, escape key, superseding navigation) and handles traversals and rollbacks of cancelled navigations. Use it instead and remove the adapter, along with the `transitionCreated` subject that only existed to feed it.

The feature is only enabled when `window.navigation` is available: `PlatformNavigation` is backed by `window.navigation` and has no server implementation, so enabling it unconditionally would break SSR and prerendering, as well as browsers without Navigation API support. Those fall back to the regular history-based `Location`, as before.

Since in-memory scrolling is enabled, the Router intercepts navigations with `scroll: 'manual'`, so scrolling is still handled by `AppScroller`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(docs-infra): use the router's platform Navigation API integration" (#71023)

Issues.Title: feat(migrations): migrate ActivatedRoute snapshot reads to route input binding
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

With withComponentInputBinding(), routed components can receive route params as inputs. Many components still inject ActivatedRoute only to read route.snapshot.paramMap.get('id'), and there's no migration to convert them.

### Proposed solution

An opt-in ng generate @angular/core:route-input-binding schematic. It replaces snapshot reads of path and query params with signal inputs (this.id()) and removes the ActivatedRoute injection once it's unused.

Only reads that are guaranteed to be equivalent are migrated:

- Input binding must already be enabled for every router setup. The migration never enables it, because doing so changes all routed components.
- The component must be rendered directly by a route and must not be used in other components' templates.
- Keys must not collide between path params, query params and route data.
- Reads must not run during construction. Reads in the constructor, in field initializers, or in methods called from them are skipped.

#### Planned follow-ups
- Move constructor reads into ngOnInit. afterNextRender isn't suitable because it doesn't run during SSR and runs only after the first render.
- Replace paramMap.subscribe(...) with effect + untracked, and paramMap.pipe(...) with toObservable(input).pipe(...).
- Convert properties derived from params (e.g. id, isEdit) into inputs or computed, rewriting their TypeScript and template references with the signal-input migration's existing passes.
- Support route data reads, and add a best-effort mode for add/edit components whose param isn't declared on every route.

#### Open question

Repeated query params (?tag=a&tag=b) bind an array, while queryParamMap.get returns the first value. Should query param reads be migrated with a documented caveat, or skipped?

### Alternatives considered

No
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "feat(migrations): migrate ActivatedRoute snapshot reads to route input binding" (#71000)

Issues.Title: feat(migrations): add migration from ActivatedRoute snapshot reads to route input binding
Issues.Body:
Adds the `route-input-binding` schematic, which replaces reads of path and query params from an injected `ActivatedRoute` snapshot with signal inputs in apps that bind route information to component inputs via `withComponentInputBinding()` or `bindToComponentInputs: true`.

A read is only migrated if the bound input is guaranteed to have the same value: the component must be routed directly, input binding must be enabled for every router setup, path params must be declared by every route that renders the component (or query params must not be bound), and keys must not collide with route data or other params. Reads in constructors and field initializers are skipped, since routed inputs are set after creation. The `ActivatedRoute` injection is removed if it's private and no longer used.

Fixes: #71000

Issues.Title: docs: add pages for the NG8011 and NG8112 extended diagnostics
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`controlFlowPreventingContentProjection` (NG8011) and `unusedLetDeclaration` (NG8112) are extended diagnostics that can be configured under `extendedDiagnostics.checks`, but neither has a details page or a row in the table on the extended diagnostics overview. Every other configurable extended diagnostic has both.

For NG8112 this also leaves a dead end. The diagnostic message ends with `Find more at https://v22.angular.dev/extended-diagnostics/NG8112` (as printed by `ngc` 22.2.0), and that URL currently serves the angular.dev fallback ("Home") page, the same page (same title and size) as for a code that doesn't exist (for example NG9999). `NG8113` renders its real page at the same kind of URL.

NG8011 is reported often and the message alone leaves questions open (see #54077 and #59398). In #59398 a maintainer reopened the issue to "improve the error message / add a dedicated error page in our documentation".

Related to #59398 (this adds the docs page only, it does not change the message)

## What is the new behavior?

- Adds `NG8011.md` and `NG8112.md` in the same format as the existing pages: example, "What's wrong with that?", "What should I do instead?", and how to suppress it.
- Adds both diagnostics to the table in `overview.md`. Prettier re-aligned the rest of the table because `controlFlowPreventingContentProjection` is now the longest name, so the other rows only change in column padding (and the header separator gets longer). `prettier --check` fails on the file without it.
- The NG8011 page describes the behavior as implemented in `TcbControlFlowContentProjectionOp`: which blocks are checked, that text counts as a root node, and that whitespace only counts with `preserveWhitespaces: true`. It recommends `<ng-container ngProjectAs="...">` as the workaround, which is what is suggested in #59398, and links to the existing `ngProjectAs` section of the content projection guide.
- The NG8112 page notes that the expression of an unused `@let` is still evaluated on every template update.

How this was verified:

- The `angular-ts` blocks were extracted from the markdown files and compiled with the released `@angular/compiler-cli@22.2.0` (`ngc`, `strictTemplates`). Only the two "problem" examples report a diagnostic (NG8011 and NG8112). The four "prefer" examples are clean.
- Behavior claims were checked against the compiler with `ngc`: both diagnostics honor `defaultCategory`, `suppress` silences them, `error` fails the build (exit 1), `@for`, `@empty`, `@case` and `@else` are all checked, blocks nested inside another element are not, and whitespace matters only with `preserveWhitespaces: true`.
- The NG8011 example was rendered with `@angular/platform-server`. Without a fix, `<h2 card-title>` ends up in the default slot. With `ngProjectAs` on a wrapping `<ng-container>`, or with the content split across two blocks, it lands in the `[card-title]` slot.
- For NG8112, the emitted JavaScript for an unused `@let` still contains the call to the expression (`ctx.compute();`).
- `prettier --check` passes for the three changed files.
- `bazel build //adev/src/content/reference/extended-diagnostics:extended-diagnostics //adev/src/content/reference/extended-diagnostics:route-nav-items` succeeds. The generated `routes.json` contains "NG8011: Control flow preventing content projection" and "NG8112: Unused `@let` declaration", the `ngProjectAs` link renders as `guide/components/content-projection#aliasing-content-for-projection`, and both new rows are present in the generated overview HTML. (Built under WSL2, since native Windows Bazel is not supported.)
- There is no test to add, as this only changes markdown. Nothing automated checks that the code in the docs still compiles, so the examples were checked by hand as described above.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

#68652 changes the wording of the NG8011 message in `oob.ts`. It touches different files, and the guidance on this page (wrap in `<ng-container ngProjectAs>` or split the block) matches what that PR adds to the message.

Issues.Title: fix(service-worker): wait for stability when registerWhenStable has no timeout
Issues.Body:
`registrationStrategy: 'registerWhenStable'` without a timeout is supposed to wait for the app to go idle before registering. It registers right away instead, during initial load, which is what the strategy exists to avoid.

With no timeout `args` is empty, so `+args[0]` is `NaN`, `setTimeout(resolve, NaN)` behaves as `setTimeout(resolve, 0)`, and that timer wins the `Promise.race` every time. `registerWhenStable:` is the same, since `+''` is 0.

It's a regression. The code was `!args[0] ? whenStable$ : merge(whenStable$, delayWithTimeout(+args[0]))` until #60657 ("pull less RxJS symbols") collapsed it into a plain `Promise.race` and dropped the `!args[0]` arm. Broken since v20.0.0. `registerWithDelay` right above still guards with `+args[0] || 0`.

The two specs covering this passed anyway: the mocked `whenStable()` returned an Observable rather than a `Promise<void>`, and `Promise.race` resolves a non-thenable immediately, so the timer never decided anything. #60657 also deleted their `tick(60000)` assertions. Both are restored here.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): report errors for malformed template literal interpolations
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The expression parser silently discards unexpected tokens inside a template literal interpolation:

- `` `p${a b}q` `` is parsed as `` `p${a}q` `` with no diagnostic (a top-level `a b` is correctly rejected).
- `` `${flags & 1}` `` is parsed as `` `${flags}` ``. Bitwise operators are documented as unsupported.
- `` `${a, b}` `` and `` `${a; b}` `` are truncated to `${a}`.
- A template literal with an interpolation that is never terminated (`` `p${a}q ``) is accepted, while `` `abc `` is rejected.

Invalid syntax is therefore turned into different, valid syntax without telling the author.

The cause is in `parseTemplateLiteral`: it used a catch-all `advance()` to consume the `}` that closes an interpolation. The same branch also consumed any other leftover token, and the lexer error token produced for an unterminated literal.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

The closing brace is consumed with the parser's existing `expectCharacter('}')`, and lexer error tokens that follow an interpolation are reported. The examples above now produce a parse error (`Missing expected }` or `Unterminated template literal`).

The check runs before `rbracesExpected` is decremented, so `skip()` still stops at the brace of the interpolation. Recovery therefore keeps every element and expression of the literal (the shape mismatch that caused #69699). Decrementing first would make recovery skip past the interpolation's `}` and drop the rest of the literal.

Verification:

- The new parser specs fail without the fix and pass with it. Reverting either half of the fix makes at least one of them fail.
- The new ngtsc spec (`should report a parse error for unexpected tokens in a template literal interpolation`) fails without the fix (it was the only failure in the full ngtsc suite) and passes with it.
- Bazel: `//packages/compiler/...`, `//packages/compiler-cli/...` (including the ngtsc suite and the compliance goldens) and `//packages/language-service/...` pass. I could not run the browser (`*_web_*`) variants locally because the browsers cannot launch in my WSL environment. The same specs pass in the Node targets.
- Parsing 8,886 templates from this repository (HTML files and inline templates) with the old and new parser gives identical diagnostics.
- A differential fuzz of about 120,000 generated template literals produced no new errors for valid Angular syntax.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Templates with malformed interpolations that were previously accepted (leftover tokens dropped, or an unterminated literal after an interpolation) now fail to compile with a parse error. Those templates compiled to something other than what was written. Valid expressions are not affected, and no template in this repository changed behavior. Please flag it if you consider this stricter validation to need a `BREAKING CHANGE` note.

## Other information

No docs change is needed: `expression-syntax.md` already lists bitwise operators and the comma operator as unsupported.

**Testing scope.** Locally (Bazel under WSL2) I ran the compiler, compiler-cli (ngtsc, compliance goldens, linker) and language-service suites, and they pass. I did not run the rest of the repository suite (core, common, forms, router and so on) or the browser (`*_web_*`) variants, so I am relying on CI for those. If CI shows a failure outside the compiler packages, the first thing to check is a template that contains a malformed `${...}` interpolation.

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

## What is the current behavior?

The js-web-frameworks benchmark uses `ɵNoopNgZone` and calls `ApplicationRef.tick()` without marking the component for checking. Issues.Title: RouteReuseStrategy: reattached child keeps providers from a destroyed parent injector
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

### Description

When a child route is detached and stored by a custom `RouteReuseStrategy`, while its component-bearing parent route is destroyed, reattaching the stored child under a newly-created parent leaves the child connected to the dependency-injection hierarchy of the previous parent instance.

Consider a parent component that provides a service:

```ts
@Component({
  providers: [ParentScopedService],
  template: '<router-outlet />',
})
class Parent {
  readonly service = inject(ParentScopedService);
}
```

and a routed child that injects the same service:

```ts
@Component({...})
class Child {
  readonly service = inject(ParentScopedService);
}
```

The reuse strategy intentionally behaves as follows:

```text
parent: shouldDetach() === false
child:  shouldDetach() === true
```

Navigation:

```text
/parent/child
→ /home
→ /parent/child
```

On the first navigation away:

1. `Child #1` is detached and stored.
2. `Parent #1` is destroyed.

When navigating back:

1. `Parent #2` is created.
2. A new `ParentScopedService #2` is created for `Parent #2`.
3. The stored `Child #1` is reattached below `Parent #2`.

The resulting component tree is therefore:

```text
Parent #2
└── Child #1
```

However, the DI state is:

```text
Parent #2 → ParentScopedService #2
Child #1  → ParentScopedService #1
```

The reused child still uses the service instance belonging to the destroyed previous parent instead of the service provided by its current parent.

In other words:

```ts
secondParent.service !== firstParent.service;

// Child was successfully reused:
secondChild === firstChild;

// But the reused child still has the old parent's service:
secondChild.service === firstParent.service;

// Expected:
secondChild.service === secondParent.service;
```

This creates an inconsistent state where a routed parent and its current routed child operate on different instances of a service scoped to that parent.

It also means that the old parent injector hierarchy remains reachable through the reused child for as long as the child is retained.

Looking at the router implementation, this appears to happen because the component's injector hierarchy is established when `RouterOutlet.activateWith()` creates the component, while `RouterOutlet.attach()` later only inserts the existing `hostView`. Reattaching the view does not appear to update the injector ancestry of the existing component.

If reattaching a stored child underneath a recreated component-bearing ancestor is intentionally unsupported, it would be useful for the router to reject or explicitly document this combination. Currently, `RouteReuseStrategy` allows this configuration and the reattachment succeeds, but leaves the component with stale parent-scoped dependencies.

This appears closely related to #20072.

That issue demonstrated the same observable behavior: a reused child continued to use a service instance belonging to a previous parent after the parent had been destroyed and recreated.

#20072 was considered possibly related to #18374, but the scenarios are different:

- #18374 is about whether the default reuse strategy should reuse a parent when the route configuration objects differ.
- This issue is about the resulting injector hierarchy after a custom `RouteReuseStrategy` has explicitly detached and successfully reattached a child while its parent was destroyed and recreated.

There is also a potential memory-retention issue here. Because the reused child continues to reference the injector hierarchy of the destroyed parent, objects reachable from that hierarchy — including parent-scoped services and potentially parts of the destroyed parent view tree — may remain strongly reachable for as long as the reused child is alive. In applications that keep detached route handles for a long time, this can effectively behave as a memory leak: destroying and recreating parent routes does not necessarily make the previous parent injector graph eligible for garbage collection.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://bolt.new/p/71539648

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
AssertionError: expected { Object (id) } to be { Object (id) } // Object.is equality

- Expected
+ Received

  ParentScopedService {
-   "id": 0.5120725349564125,
+   "id": 0.5155806087407758,
  }

 ❯ src/route-reuse.spec.ts:146:61
    144|   // FAILS:
    145|   // The reused child still resolves the service from the destroyed parent.
    146|   expect(reattachedChild.injector.get(ParentScopedService)).toBe(secondParent.injector.get(ParentScopedService));
       |                                                             ^
    147| });
    148|
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true

```

### Anything else?

Related issues:

- #20072 — `RouteReuseStrategy doesn't reuse the parent tree components`
- #18374 — `Router not reusing parent component when changing only the child route`

#20072 seems particularly relevant because it reproduces the same stale parent-scoped service behavior.

A likely workaround is to detach/reuse the highest component-bearing ancestor together with its subtree, rather than retaining a child while destroying one of its DI ancestors. Another workaround is to recreate the child and preserve its application state separately instead of retaining the child `ComponentRef`.

There does not appear to be a public API for updating the injector ancestry of an already-created component after it has been attached to a new routed parent.

With `debounce(path, 'blur')` the value is only written when the control is blurred. If the focused control is destroyed first, browsers that do not fire `blur` on removal (e.g. Safari) never write it, and the typed value is lost.

Issues.Title: Signal Forms: debounce('blur') loses the typed value when the focused input is removed
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `debounce(path, 'blur')`, the typed value is only written to the model when the control is blurred. If the focused input is removed from the DOM before it is blurred (an `@if`, a wizard step, a tab switch, a route change), the pending value is never written. The user's input is silently lost.

Steps:
1. Type into an input that uses `debounce(path, 'blur')`.
2. Press Enter, which runs `(keydown.enter)` and removes the input through `@if`. Don't click or Tab away first.
3. The model still has its old value.

Browsers:
- **Safari 26.5:** reproduces. Safari follows the HTML "focus fixup" rule and fires no `blur` when a focused element is removed, so nothing flushes the pending value.
- **Chrome:** does not reproduce, because Chrome fires `blur` right before it removes the focused element, while Angular's listener is still attached.
- **Firefox:** not tested.

Duration debounces (`debounce(path, 300)`) keep the value in every browser, because the timer still fires after the input is destroyed. Only `'blur'` mode depends on the `blur` event.

As far as I can tell, 'blur' mode only ends when the control's `blur` listener calls `markAsTouched()`, which flushes the pending sync. Nothing flushes it when the control is destroyed.

The reproduction has a "Recorder" list that shows the events in order. In Chrome there is a `blur` and a model update before the input is removed. In Safari there is neither.

Issues.Title: Server builder assets can overwrite the generated main.js entry point
Issues.Body:
### Command

`build`, `run`

### Is this a regression?

No. The server builder has copied configured assets after Webpack output since the `assets` option was released in 15.1.0.

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

No response.

### Description

`@angular-devkit/build-angular:server` copies configured assets after Webpack emits the server program, without checking whether an asset destination is already a generated file.

With a recursive asset tree copied to output `.`, an asset named `main.js` silently replaces the generated server entry point. The build reports success, and normal `node dist/server/main.js` startup executes the asset instead of the generated application bundle.

I reproduced this with an asset-only dependency update. Version 1.0.0 contains only `assets/data.json`; version 1.0.1 adds only `assets/main.js`. Neither version declares `scripts`, `main`, `exports`, `imports`, or `bin`, installation uses `--ignore-scripts`, and the application never imports the package.

Expected: the build should reject an asset/generated-output collision, or keep generated output authoritative.

Actual: the build succeeds and the final `dist/server/main.js` is byte-for-byte identical to the dependency asset. Starting it executes dependency-controlled code as the deployed server process.

### Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro

```sh
git clone https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro.git
cd angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro
./scripts/validate.sh
```

The validator runs clean → attack → restored-clean → restored-attack. Across two fresh-container runs, clean 1.0.0 always emitted and started the same genuine 782,472-byte bundle with no marker; attack 1.0.1 always emitted the exact 192-byte package asset and executed its marker. Runtime networking is disabled, and the script fails on any control mismatch.

### Exception or Error

No exception is reported. The builder reports successful bundle generation and asset copying.

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.0
@angular-devkit/build-angular: 22.2.0
Angular: 22.2.0
Node: 24.21.0
npm: 11.19.0
OS: Linux arm64 container (node:24.21.0-bookworm-slim)
```

### Anything else relevant?

The builder is deprecated but remains shipped. The default server `assets` list is empty, and exploitation requires an opt-in recursive root-output rule plus an accepted package update, build, deployment, and startup. I therefore assess this as High rather than Critical.

Current source shows the [server builder calling `copyAssets()` after successful Webpack output](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular_devkit/build_angular/src/builders/server/index.ts#L80-L126), while [`copyAssets()` writes each destination without checking generated outputs](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular_devkit/build_angular/src/utils/copy-assets.ts#L41-L60).

This is distinct from #19157 and #16670, which discuss precedence between two configured asset inputs rather than a post-Webpack asset replacing the executable generated entry point.

Should the server builder reject configured asset destinations that collide with generated output files?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Server builder assets can overwrite the generated main.js entry point" (#34195)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): avoid loading localize tools and babel in i18n inliner worker
Issues.Body:
Previously, `i18n-inliner-worker.ts` dynamically loaded `@angular/localize/tools` to invoke its `translate()` function and `Diagnostics` class. Importing `@angular/localize/tools` eagerly pulls in `@babel/core`, `@angular/compiler-cli`, and `@angular/compiler`, consuming ~180 ms of CPU latency and ~32 MB of heap per worker thread upon first translation.

Since the inliner only performs string translation replacements using AST locations already discovered via OXC, the full Babel transformation and compiler tooling bundle is unnecessary.

This updates `i18n-inliner-worker.ts` to directly import low-level runtime functions (`ɵtranslate`, `ɵisMissingTranslationError`, `ɵmakeTemplateObject`) from `@angular/localize` and manage diagnostics via a direct message array. This completely avoids loading `@angular/localize/tools` and its heavy transitive dependencies.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(@angular/build): avoid loading localize tools and babel in i18n inliner worker" (#34194)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): lazy load sourcemap remapping in i18n inliner worker
Issues.Body:
Previously, `@ampproject/remapping` was statically imported at the top level of `i18n-inliner-worker.ts`, eagerly pulling in 5 packages (`@ampproject/remapping` and 4 sub-dependencies) upon worker initialization.

In typical workflows or when sourcemaps are not requested for inlining, remapping is never executed.

This changes the import of `@ampproject/remapping` to be dynamic so that it is only loaded when a file actually requires sourcemap remapping.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(@angular/build): lazy load sourcemap remapping in i18n inliner worker" (#34193)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): lazy load sourcemap remapping in js transform worker
Issues.Body:
Previously, `@ampproject/remapping` was statically imported at the top level of `javascript-transformer-worker.ts`, eagerly pulling in 5 packages (`@ampproject/remapping` and 4 sub-dependencies) upon worker initialization.

In standard Angular CLI configurations (`ng build` and `ng serve`), vendor sourcemaps are disabled by default (`thirdPartySourcemaps = false`), causing `useInputSourcemap` to evaluate to false for all transformed `node_modules` files. As a result, sourcemap remapping is never executed in typical builds.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular/build): lazy load sourcemap remapping in js transform worker" (#34191)

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): cache transformed configuration in TypeScript compilation
Issues.Body:
When `rootFiles` are explicitly provided (e.g. in library builds), re-parsing `tsconfig.json` and traversing the project directory structure via `readConfiguration` on every incremental watch rebuild is redundant and adds measurable overhead (~200-350ms on large libraries).

This change caches the `TransformedConfiguration` in `TypeScriptCompilation` when explicit `rootFiles` are provided and invalidates the cache only when a `.json` configuration file changes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "perf(@angular/build): cache transformed configuration in TypeScript compilation" (#34192)

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): avoid loading compiler-cli and typescript in JS transform worker
Issues.Body:
Previously, `OxcLinker` imported `ConsoleLogger` and `LogLevel` directly from `@angular/compiler-cli`. Even though `@angular/compiler-cli/linker` is an isolated, lightweight runtime (depending only on `semver` and `convert-source-map`), resolving the main `@angular/compiler-cli` entry point (`bundles/index.js`) eagerly evaluated the full `ngtsc` compiler toolchain and required the 10 MB `typescript.js` bundle at the top level.

As a result, every worker isolate in the JavaScript transformer pool unnecessarily loaded TypeScript and 50+ compiler modules upon bootstrap, incurring ~150 ms of startup CPU latency and allocating ~12 MB of heap per worker thread.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "perf(@angular/build): avoid loading compiler-cli and typescript in JS transform worker" (#34189)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): ensure asset followSymlinks defaults to false
Issues.Body:
When `followSymlinks` is omitted from an asset configuration entry, its value is `undefined`. Because `tinyglobby` treats `followSymbolicLinks: undefined` as `true`, symlinked subdirectories within asset folders were traversed even though the schema documents the default as `false`.

Coerce `entry.followSymlinks` to a boolean (`!!entry.followSymlinks`) so the runtime behavior matches the documented schema default and the existing Webpack builder behavior.

Closes #34164

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): support library compilation in AngularCompilation
Issues.Body:
Adds library compilation support (`buildType: 'application' | 'library'`) to `AngularCompilation`, `TypeScriptCompilation`, `AotCompilation`, and `transformCompilerOptions`:
- Support `declarationMap`, `compilationMode`, and `paths` overrides in `CompilerOptionOverrides`.
- Configure library-specific compiler options (`declaration`, `importHelpers`, `Bundler` module resolution, external `sourceMap`, and TypeScript transpilation) when `buildType === 'library'`.
- Emit multiple files per `SourceFile` (`.js`, `.d.ts`, `.d.ts.map`) in `AotCompilation.emitAffectedFiles()` and skip application-only transformers (`replaceBootstrap`, `webWorkerTransform`, `lazyRoutesTransformer`) during library emission.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): deduplicate spurious chokidar polling change events
Issues.Body:
When  using Chokidar in polling mode, non-atomic file writes (such as open with O_TRUNC followed by write) can span across poll intervals and cause Chokidar to emit two 'change' events for a single file modification. If the initial rebuild completes quickly (e.g. in JIT mode), the trailing poll event can flush a second rebuild batch with the same file state.

Track the last known mtimeMs and size of watched files in createChokidarWatcher and ignore 'modified' events when the file's mtimeMs and size have not changed since the previous queued or flushed event.

Issues.Title: ng build --watch --preserve-symlinks dies with EMFILE when watch mode starts
Issues.Body:
Hi team,

We have one monorepo. A web app and an API both compile a shared model folder. That folder has no `package.json`. The web app reaches it through a symlink, `libs/model`, pointing at `../../model` next to the web app. The watch command is `ng build --watch --preserve-symlinks`. We need `preserveSymlinks` so that link keeps working. On 22.1.7 this watch runs fine.

After moving `@angular/cli` and `@angular/build` to 22.2.0, the bundle still completes (about 92 seconds). Then the process dies as soon as watch mode starts:

```
Watch mode enabled. Watching for file changes...

Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:267:21)
```

The stack goes through chokidar. We're on macOS, Node 24.16.0. `ulimit -n 65536` does not stop it.

22.2 uses chokidar for this case so a directory symlink is still rebuilt. That part is what #34060 fixed for #34039, and the rebuilds do show up. The new problem is everything else the watcher opens. In `setupWatcher`, `**/node_modules/**` is only added to the ignore list when `preserveSymlinks` is false. The comment says that is so `npm link` keeps working. With the flag on, chokidar calls `fs.watch` for every directory under `node_modules`. Ours is large enough that the process runs out of file handles.

This symlink is not an npm link, and it is not inside `node_modules`. Ignoring `node_modules` would still follow `libs/model` to the shared model folder. Could the watcher skip `node_modules` when `preserveSymlinks` is on, and only watch a package that was actually created with `npm link`?

We've gone back to 22.1.7 for now.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "ng build --watch --preserve-symlinks dies with EMFILE when watch mode starts" (#34185)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): skip components with a change detection strategy in the zoneless migration tool
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`categorizeFile` in the `onpush_zoneless_migration` MCP tool is meant to skip components that already declare a change detection strategy (it logs "Component file already has change detection strategy ... Skipping migration."). Its pre-filter regex looks for `changeDetectionStrategy:`, but the `@Component` metadata key is `changeDetection` (the AST check in `migrate-single-file.ts` already uses `changeDetection`). The regex never matches, so that branch is dead: every component goes into `filesWithComponents`, and when there is more than one the tool sends a `sampling/createMessage` request to the client to rank files that `migrateSingleFile` then drops by returning `null`. The final answer is right, but it costs a sampling round-trip, which some clients ask the user to approve.

## What is the new behavior?

- The regex matches `changeDetection:`, so already-migrated components are skipped and no ranking request is sent for them.
- A skipped component that imports `NgZone` is still added to `zoneFiles`. Today those components reach `analyzeForUnsupportedZoneUses` through `migrateSingleFile`; without this, fixing the regex would have stopped the tool reporting NgZone blockers in OnPush components.

New `zoneless-migration_spec.ts` (first spec for this entry point) covers:
- two components with a strategy: no sampling request (fails before the fix);
- two components without one: exactly one ranking request (control);
- an OnPush component using `NgZone.onMicrotaskEmpty`: the unsupported NgZone response is still returned (fails if the `zoneFiles` routing is removed).

`pnpm bazel test //packages/angular/cli:test` passes (272 specs).

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code), and reviewed with GitHub Copilot, which caught the NgZone case above. I checked each test fails without the change it covers.

Issues.Title: feat(@angular/build): add `prerenderFormat` option to prerender routes as `<route>.html`
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

<!-- Please check all that apply using "x". -->

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Prerendering always writes a route to `<route>/index.html`. On static hosts, this forces a choice between clean URLs and no redirects. You can't have both:

- **Clean URLs, but redirects:** links use `/<route>`. Every direct request (search engines, bookmarks, shared links) is first redirected (301/308) to `/<route>/`, and the Angular router then removes the trailing slash again.
- **No redirects, but trailing slashes everywhere:** links have to use `/<route>/`, and the app needs `TrailingSlashPathLocationStrategy` to keep the slash in the address bar.

Issue Number: #29173

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the new behavior that. -->

A new application builder option `prerenderFormat` makes both possible: clean URLs without a trailing slash, served directly with a status code 200.

- `"directory"` (default): `/foo/bar` is written to `foo/bar/index.html`, unchanged.
- `"file"`: `/foo/bar` is written to `foo/bar.html`, so hosts that serve `<route>.html` for `/<route>` respond to `/foo/bar` without a redirect.

Mirrors Astro's `build.format` (`'directory' | 'file'`); Next.js, SvelteKit and Hugo offer the same choice via `trailingSlash`/`uglyURLs`.

- The root route (after removing the `baseHref` option) stays `index.html`, so `/` and `/<locale>/` keep being served by the host's directory index.
- A route that cannot be written safely to `<route>.html` keeps `<route>/index.html`, and the build reports a warning that names the route. This applies to routes whose last segment is `index` in any casing (for example `/index`, `/Index` or `/docs/index`, whose file would be the `index.html` of the parent path), to routes whose file would be the index output of the application (such as `index.csr.html`), and to routes whose file name is already used by another route (compared case-insensitively).
- `"file"` is only considered when the build does not produce a server. The `@angular/ssr` runtime looks up prerendered pages as `<route>/index.html` (`AngularServerApp.buildServerAssetPathFromRequest`, `CommonEngine.retrieveSSGPage`), and with a server there is no redirect to avoid, since the generated `server.ts` serves static files with `redirect: false`. With `outputMode: "server"`, or `ssr` without `outputMode`, the build warns that the option is not considered and prerenders to `<route>/index.html`. The dev server does not prerender and shows no warning.
- It is a top-level option rather than part of `prerender`: when `outputMode` is set, the `prerender` option is not considered ([`options.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular/build/src/builders/application/options.ts#L265-L271)), and `outputMode: "static"` is the documented way to build a fully static application.

As suggested by @SanderElias in the issue, the option description states that not all hosting services support this. Happy to rename the option if you prefer a different name.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

As a stopgap, I built a builder (`@angular-schule/prerender-format`) that wraps `@angular/build:application`. It only works by replacing the internal `prerenderPages()` export of `@angular/build` at runtime to rename the output files, which is fragile and can break with any internal refactoring. A built-in option is the clean solution.

The option description in `schema.json` feeds the `ng build` reference on angular.dev. If this lands, I'm happy to follow up with a short section in the SSR guide ("Generate a fully static application") in angular/angular.

We now pass `resetComponentUpdates` to `createAngularSsrInternalMiddleware` and `createAngularSsrExternalMiddleware`, and trigger it when an SSR HTML transform occurs (`html:transform:pre`).

Fixes #34163

Issues.Title: docs: cross-fade between pages with view transitions
Issues.Body:
Navigating between pages in the docs app swapped the content instantly. This enables the router's `withViewTransitions()`, so browsers that support the View Transitions API cross-fade from the old page to the new one. Other browsers keep the current behavior.

Changes:
- Add `withViewTransitions({skipInitialTransition: true})` to the router config. The first page load isn't animated, since there's no previous page to transition from.
- Add a global `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule that disables the view transition animations, so those users get an instant page swap.

Checked in Chrome against the dev server, comparing against a run with `document.startViewTransition` removed to get the behavior without transitions:
- Clicking a category card runs a 250ms cross-fade of the root.
- The first page load doesn't start a transition.
- Focus still moves to the new page's `focusOnNavigation` target.
- Navigating to another page with a `#fragment` still scrolls the target heading into view, at the same position as without transitions.

Issues.Title: docs: bind route params to component inputs
Issues.Body:
The routed pages in the docs app read their route params by subscribing to `ActivatedRoute` by hand. `ComponentViewer` combined its own params with its parent's to get both `:id` and `:section`, and `ComponentCategoryList` walked `pathFromRoot` and merged the params of every level to find `:section`.

This enables `withComponentInputBinding()` so that the router passes the route params to the routed components as inputs. Nested routes already receive their parent's params, because the router's params inheritance strategy defaults to `always`, so no further router config is needed.

Changes:
- `GuideViewer`: add an `id` input and derive the guide with `computed`. An `effect` sets the page title, or redirects to `/guides` if no guide matches the id.
- `ComponentViewer`: add `id` and `section` inputs and load the doc item from them with `toObservable` and `switchMap`, which still cancels a lookup when the params change before it finishes. The child pages keep reading `componentDocItem`, so they're unchanged.
- `ComponentCategoryList`: add a `section` input and turn the summary and items into signals, updating the template to read them. An `effect` sets the page title.
- Drop the `ActivatedRoute` injections, `combineLatest` and manual param merging from these components.

Tests:
- Rewrite the `GuideViewer` spec with `RouterTestingHarness` and a real route config, and cover the redirect for an unknown guide.
- Add specs for `ComponentViewer` and `ComponentCategoryList` whose routes match the app's nesting (`:section` > sidenav > page). They cover the params reaching the inputs, the page title, and the component being reused and updated when the params change.

Issues.Title: docs: update guide viewer title when route params change
Issues.Body:
`GuideViewer` subscribed to the route params to resolve the current guide, but only set the page title once in `ngOnInit`. Since the router reuses the component when only the `:id` param changes, navigating from one guide to another in-app would update the rendered guide while leaving the browser title pointing at the previous one.

This isn't reachable today because guide-to-guide links in the markdown are absolute URLs that trigger a full page load, but it would surface as soon as an in-app link between guides is added.

Changes:
- Set the page title inside the params subscription, next to where the guide is resolved, so both stay in sync on every param emission.
- Remove the now-redundant `ngOnInit` and the `OnInit` interface.
- Tie the params subscription to the component's lifetime with `takeUntilDestroyed()`, matching the pattern used in `ComponentViewer`.
- Switch the spec's mocked `params` to a `BehaviorSubject` and add tests covering the initial title and the title after a param change.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/drag-drop): avoid rendering pre-drop order in zoneless apps
Issues.Body:
When an item is dropped, the `DropListRef` resets the DOM to its pre-drag order and emits the `dropped` event. With zone.js change detection runs synchronously when the `NgZone` is exited so the new order is rendered before the browser paints. In zoneless apps change detection is scheduled asynchronously which allows the browser to paint the stale order in between, causing the dropped item to blink.

Fixes #33837.

Issues.Body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/main/pnpm) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`11.27.0` → `11.27.1`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.27.0/11.27.1) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.27.1?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/11.27.1?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/11.27.0/11.27.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.27.0/11.27.1?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.27.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.27.1): pnpm 11.27.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.27.0...v11.27.1) #### Patch Changes - `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` now run the pnpm installed alongside them. They used to look pnpm up on `PATH`. That failed when the directory holding them was not on `PATH`, and it silently handed the call to an unrelated pnpm when one came first there [#​14803](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14803). - The `@zkochan/cmd-shim` package is now available as `@pnpm/bins.cmd-shim`. - `pnpm cache list-registries` now prints the registry URL, matching `pnpm cache view`. It printed `https%3A+registry.npmjs.org` before and prints `https://registry.npmjs.org/` now [#​15046](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15046). - `pnpm deploy` no longer installs the dependencies of the workspace root project into the deploy directory [#​6437](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6437). - Install warnings no longer carry the text of a package's deprecation notice. The warning names the deprecated package and version, and the `pnpm:deprecation` event no longer carries the notice either. `pnpm view` still shows it on request. A deprecation warning now names the newest version of the package that is not deprecated, and says when reaching it means widening the range you declared: ``` WARN deprecated foo@1.0.0. 2.3.1 is not deprecated, outside the range you declared. ``` pnpm works this out from the metadata it already fetched, so it costs no extra request. An install that reuses the lockfile without fetching metadata names no version. pnpm strips control characters from the package name and version in a deprecation warning, and from the notice `pnpm outdated --long` prints. The text sanitizer now also strips the Unicode line and paragraph separators U+2028 and U+2029. - `pnpm exec ` and `pnpm ` run from a subdirectory of a project now find the executables installed in the project's `node_modules/.bin`. The command still runs in the subdirectory. `PNPM_PACKAGE_NAME` names the project [#​5068](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5068). - `pnpm exec` and `pnpm dlx` now wait for the command to finish shutting down after `Ctrl+C`. A signal sent to pnpm alone now reaches the command, the way it does with `pnpm run`. pnpm used to exit on the interrupt and terminate the command while it was still shutting down [#​7374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7374). - Warnings about ignored environment variables in project `.npmrc` credentials now link to the npmrc documentation [pnpm/pnpm#15051](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15051). - `pnpm audit --interactive --fix=update` no longer opens a second prompt for selecting dependencies to update [#​14927](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14927). - Fixed `pnpm dedupe` requiring a second pass after bumping a direct dependency in `package.json` [pnpm/pnpm#14987](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14987). - `pnpm deploy` now writes plain versions for registry dependencies with peer dependencies in the deployed `package.json`. The deployed lockfile retains the resolved peer bindings. npm aliases keep their target package names [#​14873](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14873). - `pnpm publish` now allows a detached Git HEAD in CI, including checkouts of release tags. The working tree must still be clean. Branch and remote-history checks still apply when HEAD is attached [pnpm/pnpm#5894](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5894). - `pnpm dlx` and `pnx` now prompt to approve dependency build scripts in interactive terminals. Cached packages with pending builds also prompt for approval. Without an interactive terminal, use `--allow-build` to allow the required builds. Fixes [pnpm/pnpm#14943](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14943). - `pnpm install --force` now removes obsolete dependency links inside virtual-store packages when their dependencies change. Invalid dependency names are ignored during obsolete-link cleanup [#​15039](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15039). - `pnpm add -g` and `pnpm update -g` now ignore incomplete unrelated global package groups when every command from the replaced group is retained. Operations that could remove a global command still require complete ownership information. - Resolving a Node.js runtime now fails when unofficial-builds.nodejs.org cannot be reached. pnpm used to ignore that failure and leave the musl builds out of `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm update` then wrote a different lockfile on a machine whose network blocks the mirror [pnpm/pnpm#14813](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14813). - pnpm now deduplicates a package whose child dependency resolved an optional peer in one workspace project but not in another. Two copies of `next` could appear when only some projects could reach `styled-jsx`'s optional `babel-plugin-macros` peer [#​14800](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14800). - Fixed shell completion of package scripts for `pnpm run` and `pnpm run-script` [pnpm/pnpm#15034](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15034). Bash completion now preserves literal script names containing glob characters and shell punctuation in pnpm v11 and v12. - `pnpm sbom` now publishes a valid URL in the CycloneDX `externalReferences[].url` and the SPDX `homepage`. An npm shorthand such as `vercel/ms` or `gitlab:group/subgroup/project` is expanded to the `git+https` URL npm derives for it. An scp-style remote such as `git@github.com:vercel/ms.git` is expanded the same way. Any other URL is published in its normalized form, without embedded credentials. A value that names no repository, an email address for example, is left out. pnpm used to publish the raw value, so a shorthand produced a URL that consumers such as Dependency-Track reject [pnpm/pnpm#14773](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14773). - `pnpm setup` now describes the displayed configuration changes as "the following configuration changes." - `pnpm --version` now reports why the pnpm version a project pins cannot be installed or recorded, then prints the version of the running CLI. It used to fail, which made the command unusable where the filesystem is read-only. `pnpm --version` also honors `--store-dir` and its `--store` alias now [#​14831](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14831). - `pnpm install --force` now reinstalls dependencies when the manifest and lockfile are unchanged. It previously reported "Already up to date" without reinstalling. Files changed in `node_modules` are restored when the store content is intact. Combining `--force` with `--frozen-store` now reports a configuration conflict on repeat installs [#​919](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/919). - `pnpm install` now installs git-hosted dependencies without preparing them when their builds are explicitly denied by `allowBuilds`. Dependencies that require preparation still need an explicit allow or deny decision [pnpm/pnpm#10522](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10522). - `pnpm runtime set` and `pnpm env use` now use the pnpm version that started the command. They could run a different installed pnpm when the command was started through Corepack or another wrapper. - The install summary now names the version each dependency resolved to when `node-linker` is `hoisted`. It also lists what an install restores after `node_modules` is deleted, and both sides of a version change. The summary showed the range recorded in `package.json`, or nothing at all [#​15161](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15161). - The `@pnpm/npm-lifecycle` package is now available as `@pnpm/exec.npm-lifecycle`. - Fixed `minimumReleaseAge` making pnpm download a package's full metadata again on every install. The cached copy carried a validator the registry could not match, so pnpm could never revalidate it [pnpm/pnpm#15103](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15103). - pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a bare path, such as `./local-dep`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote, so the dependency linked to a directory that does not exist [#​11131](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11131). - pnpm now preserves scalar YAML anchors and aliases when editing `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Removing the entry that defines an anchor keeps surviving aliases valid. Entries updated to different values are written separately [#​8245](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8245). - pnpm now preserves comments and existing key order when updating `package.yaml`. New keys are appended to their mapping [pnpm/pnpm#2008](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2008). - `pnpm install --prod` no longer downloads the registry packages that only a devDependency reaches [#​881](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/881). - `pnpm update --global` no longer reinstalls a global package when its dependency graph resolves to what is already installed. It reports `Already up to date` [pnpm/pnpm#12002](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12002). - The `minimumReleaseAge` approval prompt now counts and displays each package version once [pnpm/pnpm#15083](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15083). - `pnpm run` no longer sends a script a second `SIGINT` when `Ctrl+C` is pressed in a terminal. A script that shuts down on the first `SIGINT` and exits at once on a second used to die before its shutdown finished [#​7374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7374). - pnpm now reads a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` whose `tasks` section uses a setting only pnpm 12 acts on, such as `concurrencyGroup`. A task's unrecognized fields are ignored, unless the field only differs in case from `concurrency` or `dependsOn`, which pnpm reports as a typo. The warning about unrecognized top-level settings now names `cargo`, `concurrencyGroups`, and `pipelines` as pnpm 12 settings. - `pnpm -r list --json` now prints one JSON array. It printed a separate array for each project when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` was `false`, so the output could not be parsed. `pnpm -r list` now reads each project's own modules directory when the projects keep their own lockfiles, so `--long` and `--parseable` report the packages that project installed [#​15011](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15011). - A signal sent to pnpm while it runs without a terminal, as a container runtime or a service manager does, now reaches the script even when the shell running it stays the script's parent. pnpm then waits for the script to finish shutting down. Such a signal used to end the shell at once or stay with it, and the script was never told to stop [#​7374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7374). - Fixed `minimumReleaseAge` being skipped for packages served by a registry that returns the same ETag for abbreviated and full package metadata [pnpm/pnpm#14925](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14925). - `pnpm install` now returns "Already up to date" in a workspace where `dedupeDirectDeps` left a project without a `node_modules` directory of its own. Such a project forced a full install on every run. - Installs in different projects that share a global virtual store no longer fail on Windows with `Access is denied` while repairing the same slot [#​15114](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15114). - `pnpm sbom` now emits a license value as a CycloneDX expression only when it is a valid SPDX license expression. Anything else is emitted as a CycloneDX license name [pnpm/pnpm#14786](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14786). - A dependency's own bins can no longer take over another package's bin shim. The POSIX shims pnpm generates used to look up their shell helpers on `PATH`, where a dependency's bins come first [#​14837](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14837). Reinstalling replaces the shims already in your `node_modules`. On Cygwin, MSYS2, and WSL the shims still take their Windows path conversion from `PATH`, so a dependency can still redirect them there. - POSIX bin shims now convert a Windows-form path such as `C:\node_modules\.bin\tsc` correctly. The shim mangled the backslashes in such a path and could not reach the package it runs. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#​14867](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14867). - `pnpm pack` now writes tarball entries grouped by file extension and file name, the order npm uses. Packages that ship many same-named files, such as template collections, pack much smaller [#​14766](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14766). - A command run in a project that the workspace does not include now acts on that project alone. A project is outside the workspace when it has a manifest of its own and no pattern in the `packages` setting selects it, or when a `!` pattern excludes it. ### [`v2.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol/server%402.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/compare/@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.0.0...@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.1.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​1624](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/1624) [`6032170`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/60321700871029401a2e3bed8fdf4f02c9ec3331) Thanks [@​SamMorrowDrums](https://redirect.github.com/SamMorrowDrums)! - Add request-time OAuth scope challenges for tools, resources, resource templates,
  and prompts. Each primitive's `scopeChallenge` callback receives the parsed
  request and verified authentication info, then either continues or returns the
  exact scope set for an `insufficient_scope` response. `requireScopes` provides a
  small helper for static all-of checks.

  `createMcpHandler` and Streamable HTTP transports return HTTP 403 with an
  `insufficient_scope` challenge before handler execution or SSE setup. The
  preflight is active whenever a registered primitive carries a `scopeChallenge`
  callback — there is no handler- or transport-level configuration. The
  challenge's `WWW-Authenticate` header is built by the same formatter as the
  bearer-auth 401/403 answers, and its `resource_metadata` parameter is derived
  from the verified `AuthInfo`: `requireBearerAuth` / `verifyBearerToken` now
  stamp their configured `resourceMetadataUrl` onto the `AuthInfo` they return
  (new optional `AuthInfo.resourceMetadataUrl` field), with a fallback to the
  well-known location for an HTTP(S) RFC 8707 `resource` identifier; the
  parameter is omitted when neither is available.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​2726](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2726) [`6fa4227`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/6fa42279fecaba423635072f716bbb2f6f7c77f3) Thanks [@​LuckTerence](https://redirect.github.com/LuckTerence)! - `SdkError` and `SdkHttpError` accept standard `ErrorOptions` as an optional fourth constructor argument and forward it to `Error`, so a wrapped error is reachable through the standard `Error.cause` chain. Version-negotiation probe failures (`SdkErrorCode.EraNegotiationFailed`) now use it: the underlying `TypeError: fetch failed` and the DNS or socket error beneath it surface via `error.cause`, so pino, Sentry, and `util.inspect` render `ENOTFOUND` / `ECONNREFUSED` / `ETIMEDOUT` instead of stopping at the `SdkError` ([#​2657](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/issues/2657)). The previous `error.data.cause` slot is still populated for compatibility but is deprecated and slated for removal; read `error.cause` instead.

- [#​2654](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2654) [`03842cd`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/03842cd9cae9a9b142c77d2fb65e829fc4e03eab) Thanks [@​pshah19](https://redirect.github.com/pshah19)! - Treat request id `0` as a real id. Two guards tested a `RequestId` for truthiness, so the legal JSON-RPC ids `0` and `''` were read as absent. Id `0` is not a corner case: the outbound request counter is zero-based, so it is the first id every peer assigns, which on the server→client leg is the first `sampling/createMessage`, `elicitation/create`, or `roots/list` a server sends.

  - `notifications/cancelled` carrying id `0` was ignored, and the in-flight handler ran to completion with its `AbortSignal` never fired.
  - A notification sent with `relatedRequestId: 0` wrongly passed the debounce gate (for methods opted into `debouncedNotificationMethods`). Because the pending set is keyed by method alone, a second such notification in the same tick was silently dropped rather than sent.

  Absent is now the only value that means "no id".

- [#​2668](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2668) [`3e90449`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/3e90449fd52997da43b79a536d2c19c446603cc7) Thanks [@​KKonstantinov](https://redirect.github.com/KKonstantinov)! - Stop sending `notifications/cancelled` for the `initialize` handshake. The spec is explicit that a client MUST NOT attempt to cancel its `initialize` request, but the outbound cancel path fired for any in-flight request: aborting the `AbortSignal` passed to `connect()`, or letting the handshake hit its timeout, put a forbidden cancellation on the wire naming the initialize request id.

  The local behaviour is unchanged — the caller's promise still rejects with the same abort/timeout error, and `connect()` still tears the connection down. Only the wire notification is suppressed. Every other method keeps the existing cancellation path.

- [#​2698](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2698) [`7b781ed`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/7b781ed4e25355a25d15974f3c76de81299694ed) Thanks [@​maxisbey](https://redirect.github.com/maxisbey)! - Read Streamable HTTP request bodies with a size limit. Every SDK-owned body read —
  `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` (and the Node transport built on it),
  `createMcpHandler`, `toNodeHandler`, and `createMcpHonoApp`'s JSON pre-parse — now stops at
  4 MiB by default (the limit the legacy SSE transport already uses; the Express adapter and stdio
  bound their reads too) and answers `413 Payload Too Large` before anything is parsed.
  `toWebRequest` (when it reads the Node stream itself) now rejects once the body exceeds the
  limit with an error whose `name` is `'RequestBodyTooLargeError'` and `status` is `413`, and
  `toNodeHandler` answers that with `413`; hand-wired callers of `toWebRequest` should handle the
  rejection or pass a pre-parsed body, and `isLegacyRequest` reports such a request as non-legacy
  so the modern handler answers it. JSON-RPC batch arrays are limited to 100 messages; a longer
  batch is answered `400` / `-32600` and none of it is dispatched.

  The limit is configurable with a new `maxRequestBodySize` option (bytes, default
  `DEFAULT_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE` = 4 MiB, exported from `@modelcontextprotocol/server`) on
  `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransportOptions`, `CreateMcpHandlerOptions` (forwarded to its
  stateless legacy leg; `isLegacyRequest` and `legacyStatelessFallback` take the same option),
  `CreateMcpHonoAppOptions`, and `ToNodeHandlerOptions` / `ToWebRequestOptions` (the adapter's
  bound applies before the handler's, so raise both). The bounded reader is exported as
  `readRequestBody` for adapter authors. Hosts that pre-parse the body and pass it as
  `parsedBody` skip the SDK's read and its size limit entirely; the batch bound applies either way.

  `createMcpHonoApp` and `createMcpExpressApp` now run their Host/Origin validation before the
  JSON body parser, so a request from a disallowed Host or Origin with an invalid JSON body is
  answered `403` rather than `400`, and its body is not read.

- [#​2590](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2590) [`75dc7ea`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/75dc7ea6e2913e1ac37d4f06eec62cd5cfac9e7a) Thanks [@​davidpavlovschi](https://redirect.github.com/davidpavlovschi)! - Reject a modern (2026-07-28) POST that omits the required `MCP-Protocol-Version` header.

  `createMcpHandler` accepted a request whose body carried a valid per-request `_meta`
  envelope but whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header was absent: the request was classified
  modern, dispatched, and answered `200` — tool handlers ran. Only the *mismatch* case
  (header present, disagreeing with the body) was rejected, so of the standard headers
  SEP-2243 requires on a modern POST, presence was enforced for `Mcp-Method` (and for
  `Mcp-Name` on the methods that mirror `params.name` / `params.uri`) but not for
  `MCP-Protocol-Version`.

  Such a request is now refused with `400 Bad Request` and JSON-RPC `-32020`
  (`HeaderMismatch`), matching the shape the sibling missing-header cells already emit and
  echoing the request id — per the Streamable HTTP spec, which requires the header on every
  POST and lists a missing required standard header as a `HeaderMismatch` failure. The
  spec's allowance to treat a header-less request as `2025-03-26` is available only to a
  server that also serves pre-2025-06-18 clients, and permits routing it to *legacy*
  handling — never serving it as 2026-07-28; under `legacy: 'reject'` the requirement is
  unconditional.

  Era classification is deliberately unchanged and stays body-primary: a proxy that strips
  the header still must not change the era, so such a request is still *classified* modern
  and is refused one rung later, at `standard-header-validation` — the same rung that
  already answers a missing `Mcp-Method`. Legacy-era traffic is untouched, notifications
  are unaffected, body-less `GET` / `DELETE` session operations are method-routed before
  any header validation, and stdio serving (which has no HTTP headers) is not involved.

  Clients built with this SDK always send the header, so no first-party client is affected;
  hand-rolled clients that omitted it must add it.

- [#​2494](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2494) [`6a05402`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/6a054025e8cebaecead76fb51d92ba3974e8d091) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `StdioServerTransport` now closes itself and fires `onclose` when its stdin ends or closes. The stdio binding says servers "SHOULD exit promptly when their standard input is closed" — stdin EOF is the primary graceful-shutdown signal, and on some platforms (notably Windows, where no signal is delivered when the parent goes away) the only reliable one. Previously the transport listened only for `data` and `error`, so when an MCP client hung up its end of the pipe (window closed, session restarted, host crashed) the server never noticed: `onclose` never fired, nothing tore down, and server processes accumulated as zombies until killed by hand. The transport now attaches `end`/`close` listeners on stdin that close the transport (idempotently — `onclose` still fires exactly once if `close()` is also called), so `Server`/`McpServer` and `serveStdio` tear down through the existing `onclose` chain and a well-behaved server process exits naturally. Requests still in flight when stdin ends are aborted (their handlers observe `signal.aborted`) and their responses are not written: EOF means the client has hung up and is no longer waiting. A client that wants answers keeps stdin open until it has read them.

- [#​2613](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2613) [`70de0c8`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/70de0c8b569b0d664a56b90be2f141d1d1645880) Thanks [@​jwcarman](https://redirect.github.com/jwcarman)! - Emit and validate the `Mcp-Name` header for tasks requests per SEP-2663's Streamable HTTP binding: the client transport now mirrors `params.taskId` into `Mcp-Name` on `tasks/get` / `tasks/update` / `tasks/cancel` (previously omitted, causing conforming servers to reject every task poll with `-32020 HeaderMismatch`), and the server-side standard-header validation cross-checks it via the same shared `MCP_NAME_HEADER_SOURCE` table.

  On the server, `createMcpHandler` now answers a modern (2026-07-28) `tasks/get` / `tasks/update` / `tasks/cancel` POST that omits `Mcp-Name`, or whose header disagrees with `params.taskId`, with `400` / `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) at the `standard-header-validation` rung, the same treatment `tools/call` / `prompts/get` / `resources/read` already get. Legacy-era (2025-11-25) tasks traffic is unaffected. Clients built with this SDK release send the header; hand-rolled clients that omitted it must add it.
